title: The Sunk Cost Effect
text: “Gyaaaaah!?”
Itsuki, realizing he was completely naked, let out a scream and crouched down to hide his body, I say.
“W-well, that makes sense. Right after we turned into this form, our clothes came off.”
“If you don’t think about where you cast it, you end up like Itsuki.”
“Why am I the one in this position!? This kind of thing is supposed to be Motoyasu-san’s job, isn’t it!”
Just what position do I occupy in Itsuki’s mind, I wonder?
“In Motoyasu-kun’s case, wouldn’t he stand there completely naked without any shame, proud as a statue?”
“No doubt about it.”
“No doubt about it, nano.”
“HAHAHA! Something like this is nothing at all, I say! Shall I do it right now?”
Since we’d obtained the magic to return to our original forms, our goal had been achieved, I say.
“You don’t need to do it!”
“Fueeeeh……”
“Motoyasu-san would definitely actually do it! This calls for… an emergency evacuation! Four Fairy Morph!”
Itsuki turned back into his Riska form again, I say. After finally managing to return to human form, what on earth had come over him?
“I’m hurrying back to the nearest portal and heading over there!”
And with that, Itsuki dashed off briskly, found a portal, and came back, I say.
“Phew… somehow I managed to make it back. It’s good that I’m back, but why is the magic we’re after in such a half-baked location!”
“Yeah, exactly! Isn’t it usually supposed to be at the very end!”

“Maybe there are places set up that you can only reach as a human, or maybe it opened because we cleared some specific mechanism beforehand? There was something that looked like a hint drawn on the door before it opened.”
“…Perhaps it’s because we cleared the previous dungeon or something…”
“That seems likely.”
Ren, arms crossed, agreed with Itsuki’s opinion with a look of dissatisfaction, I say.
“Well, we’ve gotten the magic we were after, so shall we wrap this up and head home?”

Indeed. Goal achieved, I say. At the same time, we’d also learned magic that let us transform into pioneer-creature form at will, I say. With this, I could get Father, in his human form, to pet me without any hesitation! He would surely pet me! Even Father, whom I couldn’t save from that false accusation, would surely pet me! Because that’s the kind of person Father is, I say!
So, having achieved our goal, we were about to head back when Ren and Itsuki fell silent, I say.
“We’ve come this far! I’m going to go all the way to the depths of this dungeon and investigate everything there is to find!”
“Yeah, exactly! It turned us into these forms just to lead us here! We can’t just leave without investigating everything!”

“Let’s go!” With that, Ren and Itsuki raised their hands as if demanding to head out immediately, I say. “Ta-daa!” Ren declared, setting off at once without delay, I say. Father let out a light sigh, looking at the two of them the way one might look at children.
“Do you two know about the sunk cost effect? We’ve already achieved our goal, you know.”

I knew about it, I say. Translated into Japanese, it’s “sunk cost.” It’s the psychological effect where you try to recover costs or effort you’ve already irrecoverably spent. In this case, we were in a state of having spent tremendous effort without obtaining what we were after. Even though cutting our losses there would minimize the damage, we’d become unable to pull back. In this instance, all the hardship of becoming pioneer-creatures had only netted us the magic to return to normal. Since we’d picked up various things along the way, I thought we’d gained more than enough to be worth the trouble. But Ren and Itsuki still couldn’t let go, and were pushing forward regardless.
“If you think all the humiliation and hardship we’ve been through gets settled just by turning back into humans, you’re dead wrong!”
“I don’t not understand the feeling, but Itsuki, you have a job as an instructor at magic school, you know.”
“Ugh… I know that! I’m going to tell my students about this adventure in class!”
“Well, that’s one way to put it……”
Separate from before, Ren and Itsuki were now showing renewed motivation, I say.
“So basically, since the experience efficiency is good and there’s a chance of finding rare items, both Ren and Itsuki were secretly motivated after all.”
“From Melromarc’s perspective, having them investigate is extremely helpful.”
“It seems like a place that could be useful in future loops too, so let’s remember it, nano.”
Fiancée and Rival remarked, I say.
“Naofumi-san, you’ll be deployed too for the places only Peckuls can enter!”
“Yeah, yeah. Anyway, I’ll go get everyone’s clothes.”

And so, it was decided that whenever we had time off led by Ren and Itsuki, conquering dungeons on Cal Mira Island would become a regular habit, I say. We ended up clearing every dungeon hidden deep within each island that could only be entered in fairy form.
“Well, the incident’s resolved. I’m glad Itsuki-kun could turn back. That’s a relief for the future’s sake too.”
“So how does it turn out in the end? Does it become some kind of future energy source?”
Father asked Rafuemon, I say.
“Actually, you see, the energy obtained here ends up being put to effective use in the future. The story of its beginning goes that the heroes restored the sealed energy.”
Perhaps because he believed the future had now been confirmed, Rafuemon affirmed it.
“Maybe Rafumi was something Ren-kun developed using the energy from here?”
“Who knows. Either way, it looks like we’ll be sticking with this until Ren and Itsuki, unable to pull back, are satisfied.”
“Indeed, I say!”

And so, one after another, we cleared the dungeons. There were sometimes mechanisms that could only be progressed through as humans, I say. The attention to detail was impressive. While clearing them, we were granted all sorts of abilities as fairies, I say. Eventually, we found ourselves arriving past the point where we’d defeated the boss deep within the dungeon, King Calmar Pengu.
“This must be the last one!”

Itsuki said, looking toward the room beyond where we’d defeated the boss, I say. In the room ahead… there was a device that played fanfare, a stone monument, and a mural painted on the wall, I say. Furthermore… there was even equipment installed that looked like something Doctor would tinker with, I say. When we entered the room, flower petals danced through the air as a lively fanfare rang out.
“Feels like a ‘congratulations on clearing’ kind of thing.”
“First, let’s check the monument. This one also has text written that only heroes can read.”
“Let’s see, let’s see……”
The monument had text written on it like this, I say.

『If this monument is being read, that’s proof that you’ve accomplished everything in this dungeon, pen! We celebrate you making it this far, pen! This dungeon has drops that strengthen equipment called Sacred Weapons and Spirit Tools, so please keep searching, pen. And as a clear reward here, we’ve recorded the method for the limit-breaking Class Up right here, pen. It’s best read after giving a special core stone to the Order Guardian’s kin, the Dragon, pen.』
And so… the method for the limit-breaking Class Up was recorded right there, I say.
“Um… seems like we can learn the method for the limit-breaking Class Up here too.”
“So this is the official route to obtain it!?”
“That’s way too late!”
Ren and Itsuki, veins bulging, were fuming with anger, I say. The reward being pointless was really something else, I say.
“Killing Leludia is definitely still faster, nano~”
“Well… but maybe it was left here in case even that core stone had been lost over the long course of history?”
The text on the monument still continued, I say.

『Now then, we’d still love to keep building and pioneering all sorts of things, but it’s about time for us to set off in search of new lands, a new world… new frontiers to pioneer, pen. We hope that this place, all of these islands, and their revitalization will become of help to the Sacred Weapon heroes when the time comes, pen. So, farewell, peeen.』
That’s the text that was engraved there, I say.
“That ‘pen’ ending…”
“…I wonder if it was the Peckuls who wrote this. Maybe at other pioneer sites it’s written with ‘pyon’ or ‘chu’ or ‘wan’ instead?”
“Well, now that we’ve come this far, should we just stubbornly go make the rounds of the other pioneer sites too?”

Ren’s eyes seemed to be bloodshot, I say. Had he really taken such a liking to this place? For what it’s worth, when I asked Father about it, apparently Ren had actually grown quite fond of this dungeon for its excellent experience point yield, I say.
